s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin lesions with hyperkeratotic plaques
salient_findings: Pruritic lesions on the scrotum and buttock
Annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with atrophic center and elevated edge
Hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, and parakeratotic columns on histopathology
key_facts: Lesions located on scrotum, buttock, groin, and intergluteal cleft
Previous treatment at local clinic with little improvement
No family history of similar skin problems
Normal or negative routine blood work, syphilis serologies, and HIV testing
Histopathological examination revealed hyperkeratosis and parakeratotic columns
Perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis

shortlist.label: Darier's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and dyskeratotic keratinocytes match this rare genetic disorder

shortlist.label: Grover's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic lesions and hyperkeratosis are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Annular plaques with atrophic centers and parakeratotic columns are characteristic of porokeratosis

shortlist.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pruritic lesions and hyperkeratosis are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes are consistent with psoriasis

raw.rationale: The presence of hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, parakeratotic columns (cornoid lamella), and dyskeratotic keratinocytes in the histopathological examination are characteristic features of porokeratosis, which best explains the key facts without contradiction.

rejected.label: Darier's disease
rejected.why: While it can present with hyperkeratotic lesions, Darier's disease typically has a family history and distinct histopathological features such as suprabasal acantholytic dyskeratosis, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Grover's disease
rejected.why: Grover's disease is characterized by sudden onset of pruritic papules, which does not match the 10-year history of lesions in this case.

rejected.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
rejected.why: Lichen simplex chronicus is a condition that results from chronic scratching, leading to lichenification, which is not the primary feature described in this case.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: While psoriasis can present with hyperkeratotic plaques, the specific histopathological features and the location of the lesions in this case are more suggestive of porokeratosis.
